notes: Item 3 (owner criterion): holds. The factor base is {P : x(P) in V minus 0}, V = F2-span{1..z^(d-1)}. Each trial (a Frobenius conjugate of a random-walk anchor with known log) builds the n x (3d-1) F2 Weil-descent system of S3 = p^2 + xR p + xR^2 s^2 + b in the symmetric coordinates (s,p) in V x span{1..z^(2d-2)}, solves it by Gaussian elimination, enumerates the affine solution set, splits each (s,p) by the linear system x1^2 + s x1 = p over F2[z]_{<d}, keeps x1, x2 in V, fixes signs and re-verifies the relation by group addition. col_of_x is a dense membership/index array over V, not a table of previously seen points; there are no collisions. Linear algebra mod r is union-find with signed offsets, which is valid here because every relation has at most 2 terms. Caveats: (i) m = 2 makes the descent F2-linear, so there is no Groebner/F4 step and its cost is polynomial per trial, but the trial count is about 2^(n-d+1) ~ 2^(2n/3), so the exponent is above rho; measured trials slope 0.6465/n vs rho additions 0.3771/n, and IC/rho wall rises from 3.6 (n = 13) to 36,440 (n = 41). (ii) Kernel enumeration is capped at 2^12 (completeness-losing only). (iii) Relations only link factor-base points whose cofactor components cancel; classes are anchored by the E(F2) point x = 1 and by 2-torsion classes, so applicability depends on h. (iv) Trial generation uses Koblitz Frobenius conjugates, as the F4 arm also does. n = 37 (h = 596): PROTOCOL lists it as a moderate-cofactor check rung but states no time limit or stopping rule for it. Its stated limit is that large cofactors fragment the relation graph (named for N83, h ~ 1.1e9). From the frozen code: a relation e1 P1 + e2 P2 = R with R in <G> forces e1 c1 + e2 c2 = 0 in Z/596, so edges stay inside the ~299 classes {+-c}, about 6.9 of K ~ 2048 columns each. Off the 2-torsion classes every relation is balanced, so a root is determined only via a known anchor (x = 1 gives the order-4 class; 2-torsion classes via unbalanced cycles). That leaves max(determined, largest component) at a few dozen columns, far below 0.9K = 1843, so the while-loop cannot terminate. The operator stop at 99 s (rc = 143, no rows) is therefore consistent with the code and with the stated limit in substance. It is a post-hoc stop, not a pre-registered one. It is not a measurement and must be reported as not applicable as built, not as negative evidence; it does not enter the cofactor <= 4 fit by the protocol's own rung rule. Limitations: (a) Validated first from the working tree, then confirmed byte-identical to commit e80d9914c; the raw_data sha256 pins bind this report to those bytes. (b) The protocol improvement rule compares the IC trials slope (13 <= n <= 41) with the F4 log2 word-XOR slope (n = 13, 19, 23), which is a cross-unit comparison over different n ranges. Like-for-like checks, not headlines: IC trials slope over n <= 23 = 0.6270; IC counted ic_gauss_xors slope = 0.8477 (n <= 23) and 0.7795 (13..41). Both stay below the F4 1.0790, so the direction holds, but the F4 arm was measured in a separate 2026-10-05 session. (c) fit.json bootstrap intervals were not recomputed (resampling-dependent; not headlines). (d) Wall times are L0, from one shared container. (e) The n = 41 rung has 4 targets. (f) No planted-fault negative control: soundness rests on per-relation group re-verification and per-target scalar verification against the secret. (g) A pass means the receipt is admissible. It does not by itself establish a leaderboard improvement; that also needs the replay certificate and the matched rho reference with the 5a band.
